Nicholas Anthony Buoniconti (December 15, 1940 – July 30, 2019) was an American professional football player. He was a middle linebacker in the American Football League (AFL) and National Football League (NFL). He played for the Boston Patriots and Miami Dolphins. He won two Super Bowls with the Dolphins. Buoniconti was added into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2001. Buoniconti died on July 30, 2019, in Bridgehampton, New York, at the age of 78. After his death, an autopsy revealed that Buoniconti had been suffering from chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE).

Nicholas Comoroto (born April 22, 1991) is an American professional wrestler. He currently wrestles for All Elite Wrestling (AEW) and their sister promotion Ring of Honor (ROH). Comoroto has also made appearances in EVOLVE, WWE, and New Japan Pro-Wrestling (NJPW), Impact Wrestling, and WWE. In WWE, he was known by the ring name Nick Ogarelli. On the October 13, 2020 episode of Dark, Comoroto made his AEW debut in a loss to Darby Allin. On the January 26, 2021 episode of Dark, Comoroto earned his first victory in AEW when he teamed with Dustin Rhodes and QT Marshall to defeat Ryan Nemeth, Shawn Dean and Vary Morales. At Double or Nothing, Comoroto entered the Casino Battle Royal but the match was won by Jungle Boy. On May 30, 2024 episode of ROH on HonorClub, Comoroto and Jacoby Watts challenged The Undisputed Kingdom (Matt Taven and Mike Bennett) for their ROH World Tag Team Championships in a proving ground match but were unsuccessful in winning the championships.

Nicholas John Collison (born October 26, 1980) is a retired basketball player for the Oklahoma City Thunder of the National Basketball Association. His jersey number (#4) is the only one the team has retired since relocating to Oklahoma City. He is nicknamed "Mr. Thunder" for his loyalty to the team. During college, he played for the Kansas Jayhawks, who also retired his jersey number. He was selected 12th overall in the 2003 NBA Draft by the Seattle Supersonics, which relocated to Oklahoma City in 2008 and changed their name to the Thunder. While he never won a NBA championship as a player, he won one as an executive of the Thunder when they won their first championship in the 2024-25 season.

Nick DeSimone (born November 21, 1994) is an American professional ice hockey defenseman. He currently plays for the Utah Mammoth of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Calgary Flames and New Jersey Devils. Before playing in the NHL, DeSimone played three years with the Union Garnet Chargers of ECAC Hockey. He was not drafted by an NHL team. On July 15, 2015, DeSimone signed a two-year, $1,85 million entry-level contract to join the San Jose Sharks of the National Hockey League (NHL). He never played a game for the Sharks. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate San Jose Barracuda where he played parts of five seasons. On July 12, 2019, DeSimone signed a two-year contract to stay with the Sharks. On April 12, 2021, the Sharks traded DeSimone along with Mattias Janmark to the Vegas Golden Knights in exchange for a 2022 fifth-round pick. He was loaned out and sent down to play for the Rochester Americans. On July 17, the Knights traded DeSimone along with a 2022 fourth-round draft pick to the New York Rangers in exchange for Brett Howden. He never played a game for the Rangers. On July 28, 2021, DeSimone signed a one-year contract to join the Calgary Flames. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliates Stockton Heat and Calgary Wranglers. On July 13, 2022, DeSimone signed a two-year contract to stay with the Flames. On November 7, 2022, the Flames called him up and DeSimone made his NHL debut in a 4–3 overtime loss against the New York Islanders. On November 4, 2023, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Yegor Sharangovich goal in a 6–3 win against the Seattle Kraken. On December 21, DeSimone scored his first NHL goal against Lukáš Dostál in a 3–0 win against the Anaheim Ducks. On January 24, 2024, the Flames placed DeSimone onto waivers and his contract was picked up by the New Jersey Devils the next day. On June 24, DeSimone signed a one-year contract to stay with the Devils. On January 4, 2025, the Devils placed DeSimone onto waivers and his contract was picked up by the Utah Hockey Club the next day. On May 30, DeSimone signed a one-year, $800,000 contract to stay with the now-Utah Mammoth.

Nicholas Foligno (born October 31, 1987) is an American-Canadian professional ice hockey winger. He currently plays for the Minnesota of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Ottawa Senators, Columbus Blue Jackets, Toronto Maple Leafs, Boston Bruins, and Chicago Blackhawks. Foligno is a one-time King Clancy Memorial Trophy winner, winning in 2017. He is also a one-time All-Star game, being named one in 2015. Before playing in the NHL, Foligno played three season with the Sudbury Wolves of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He was drafted 28th overall by the Ottawa Senators of the 2006 NHL entry draft. On March 21, 2007, Foligno signed an entry-level contract to join the Senators. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliates Binghamton Senators. On October 3, 2007, Ottawa called him up and Foligno made his NHL debut in a 4–3 overtime win against the Toronto Maple Leafs. On October 18, 2007, Foligno scored his first NHL goal against Carey Price in a 4–3 win against the Montreal Canadiens. On July 21, 2010, Foligno signed a two-year, $2.4 million contract to stay with the Senators. On July 1, 2012, the Senators traded Foligno to the Columbus Blue Jackets in exchange for Marc Methot. On July 5, Foligno signed a three-year, $9.15 million contract to stay with the Jackets. On December 31, 2014, Foligno signed a six-year, $33 million contract to stay with the Jackets. On January 10, 2015, Foligno was selected to play in his first NHL All-Star game. On April 4, 2015, he recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 5–3 win against the Pittsburgh Penguins. On May 20, the team named Foligno as the sixth captain in Blue Jackets franchise history. On April 11, 2021, the Jackets traded Foligno to the Toronto Maple Leafs in exchange for a 2021 first-round draft pick and a 2022 fourth-round draft pick. He played seven regular season games, as well as, recording one assist in 4 playoff games with the Leafs. On July 28, 2021, Foligno signed a two-year, $7.6 million contract to join the Boston Bruins. He played two seasons with the Bruins. On June 26, 2023, the Bruins traded Foligno along with Taylor Hall to the Chicago Blackhawks in exchange for Ian Mitchell and Alec Regula. The next day, Foligno signed a two-year, $7.6 million contract to join the Blackhawks. On September 18, 2024, the team named Foligno as the 36th captain in Blackhawks franchise history. On March 6, 2026, the Blackhawks traded Foligno to the Minnesota Wild in exchange for future considerations. On July 2, Foligno signed a one-year, $900,000 contract to stay with the Wild. Foligno comes from a hockey family. His father Mike played fifteen seasons in the NHL and his younger brother Marcus is his Wild teammate. Foligno is a Christian.

Nick Leddy (born March 20, 1991 in Eden Prairie, Minnesota) is a professional ice hockey defenseman that currently plays for the New York Islanders of the National Hockey League (NHL). He was drafted with the 16th overall pick by the Minnesota Wild in the 2009 NHL Entry Draft. He began his hockey career when he played at the University of Minnesota with the Golden Gophers. He was drafted by the Wild and was traded to the Chicago Blackhawks along with Kim Johnsson for Cam Barker on February 12, 2010. He played his first NHL game on October 8, 2010 against the Colorado Avalanche and scored his first NHL goal on October 11, 2010 against Ryan Miller of the Buffalo Sabres. On June 24, 2013, He won the Stanley Cup with the Blackhawks after they defeated the Boston Bruins 4 games to 2 in the 2013 Stanley Cup Finals.

Nicholas Paul Punto (born November 8, 1977) is an American major league baseball player. He plays for the Los Angeles Dodgers. Punnto was born in San Diego, California. He used to play for the Boston Red Sox.

Nicholas Nicholie "Nick" Koback (July 19, 1935 – January 23, 2015) was a Polish-American professional baseball player. His career spanned eight seasons, three of which were spent with the Major League Baseball (MLB) Pittsburgh Pirates from 1953 through 1955. Koback died January 23, 2015 in Hartford, Connecticut, aged 79.

Nicholas Hilmy Kyrgios (born 27 April 1995) is an Australian professional tennis player. As of March 2020, he is ranked No. 39 in the world in men's singles by the Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) and is the second highest-ranked Australian in the ATP rankings. Kyrgios has won six ATP titles and has reached eight ATP finals, including the 2017 Cincinnati Masters. In his junior career, Kyrgios won the boys' singles event at the 2013 Australian Open and the boys' doubles event at the 2013 Wimbledon Championships. During his professional career, he reached the quarterfinals of the 2014 Wimbledon Championships and the quarterfinals of the 2015 Australian Open. He is only the third player, after Dominik Hrbaty and fellow Australian Lleyton Hewitt, to have beaten Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic the first time he played each of them. Kyrgios was born in Canberra. His father is Greek and his mother is Malay. He lives in Nassau, Bahamas.

Nick Mourouzis (April 16, 1937 – September 16, 2020) was an American football player and coach. He was the head football coach at DePauw University in Greencastle, Indiana from 1981 to 2003. He had a winning record of 133–82–4. As a college football player, Mourouzis was a starting quarterback at Miami University in Oxford, Ohio. Mourouzis was born in New Philadelphia, Ohio. Mourouzis died on September 16, 2020 from COVID-19 in Greencastle, Indiana at the age of 83.

Nicholas David Pope (born 19 April 1992) is an English footballer. He plays as a goalkeeper for Premier League club Newcastle United and the England national team. Pope started his career in Ipswich Town's youth teams. He joined Bury Town after being released at age 16. He signed for League One club Charlton Athletic in 2011, before being loaned to Harrow Borough, Welling United, Cambridge United, Aldershot Town, York City, and Bury. Pope joined Premier League club Burnley in 2016 and made his English debut two years later. He joined Newcastle United in 2022. Nick Lardis (born July 8, 2005) is a Canadian professional ice hockey winger. He currently plays for the Chicago Blackhawks of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Lardis played two seasons with the Peterborough Petes, one season with the Hamilton Bulldogs, and one season with the Brantford Bulldogs of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He had a successful time with the Bulldogs. He finished the 2024-25 season, scoring 71 goals and recording 46 assists for 117 points. For his effort, Lardis won the Jim Mahon Memorial Trophy for being the OHL's top-scoring right winger and was named to the First All-Star Team and CHL Second All-Star Team. He was drafted 67th overall by the Chicago Blackhawks in the 2023 NHL entry draft. On December 13, 2025, Lardis made his NHL debut in a 4–0 loss against the Detroit Red Wings. On December 20, Lardis scored his first NHL goal against Leevi Meriläinen in a 6–2 loss against the Ottawa Senators.

Nicklaus Perbix (born June 15, 1998) is an American professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Nashville Predators of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Tampa Bay Lightning. Before playing in the NHL, Perbix played one season with the Omaha Lancers of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and four years with the St. Cloud State Huskies of the National Collegiate Hockey Conference (NCHC). He had a successful time with his teams. He won named to the All-NCHC First Team. He was drafted 169th overall by the Tampa Bay Lightning in the 2017 NHL entry draft. On March 31, 2022, Perbix signed a one-year entry-level contract to join the Lightning. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Syracuse Crunch. On October 18, 2022, the Lightning called him up and Perbix made his NHL debut in a 3–2 loss against the Philadelphia Flyers. On October 26, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Mikhail Sergachev goal in a 4–2 win against the Anaheim Ducks. On November 5, Perbix scored his first NHL goal against Eric Comrie in a 5–3 win against the Buffalo Sabres. On January 2, 2023, Perbix signed a three-year, $2.25 million contract to stay with the Lightning. On July 1, 2025, Perbix signed a two-year, $5.5 million contract to join the Nashville Predators.
Nick Royle (born 1983) is a current England Rugby Sevens International rugby union player. He plays as a winger. He has played for Warrington, Widnes Vikings, Sale Sharks and Fylde.

Nicholas "Nick" Thompson Swisher (born November 25, 1980 in Columbus, Ohio) is an American baseball player. On December 23, 2012, Swisher agreed to a four-year, $56 million contract with the Cleveland Indians. The deal became official on January 3, 2013. Swisher is the son of former Major League Baseball player, Steve Swisher. He is married to actress Joanna García.

Nick Young (born June 1, 1985 in Los Angeles, California) is an American basketball player that currently plays for the Denver Nuggets of the NBA. He was selected by the Washington Wizards with the 16th pick in the 1st round of the 2007 NBA draft. Young played four seasons with the Wizards before being traded to the Los Angeles Clippers for a future second-round pick on March 15th, 2012. He went to University of Southern California for college and played basketball with the USC Trojans.

Nicholas Yakich (18 January 1940 – 28 May 2019) was an Australian rugby league player. He played as a winger. He played for the Manly Warringah Sea Eagles in the New South Wales Rugby League premiership competition, between 1960 and 1966. He also played for New South Wales in 1965. He was also selected for the Australian national squad, but never made the first team. He retired due to a knee injury. Yakich was born in Innisfail, Queensland. He died on 28 May 2019, at the age of 79.

Nicholas Peter Volpe (February 23, 1926 – August 21, 2021) was a Canadian football player. He played for the Toronto Argonauts from 1949 until 1952. He won the Grey Cup with the Argonauts in 1950. Volpe was born in Toronto, Ontario. Volpe died in Toronto on August 21, 2021 at the age of 95.

Nicholas Lou Saban Jr. (; born October 31, 1951) is a former American football coach. He was the head football coach at the University of Alabama from 2007 to 2023. Before that, Saban was head coach of the National Football League's Miami Dolphins, Louisiana State University (LSU), Michigan State University, and the University of Toledo. Saban is known to be the greatest coach in college football history. In 2024, Saban was added to the Alabama Sports Hall of Fame.After leaving his position at Alabama to coach at Auburn on January 11th. He is now a analyst for Auburn Tigers On January 10, 2024, Saban announced that he was retiring from coaching. He is currently a studio analyst for college football for ABC. Saban was born in Fairmont, West Virginia. He graduated from Monongah High School in the small community of Monongah, West Virginia. Saban is of Croatian ancestry. In 1975, Saban received his master's degree for sports administration from Kent State.

Nicholas Wayne Finley (born July 10, 2005) is an American professional wrestler. He currently wrestles for All Elite Wrestling (AEW) and their sister promotion Ring of Honor (ROH) under the ring name Nick Wayne. He is a member of The Patriarchy stable. Wayne has also made appearances in Game Changer Wrestling (GCW) and DEFY Wrestling. In AEW, Wayne has been a one-time AEW World Trios Champion. In DEFY, he was a DEFY World Champion. In GCW, he was a one-time GCW Tag Team Champion. At DEFY's 5th Anniversary Show, Wayne challenged Christopher Daniels for the DEFY World Championship but was unsuccessful. After the match, his friend Darby Allin came out to the ring and offered Wayne a contract to become a member of the All Elite Wrestling (AEW) roster. On the July 12, 2023 episode of Dynamite, Wayne made his AEW debut in a loss to Swerve Strickland. It was two days after Wayne had turned 18. On the July 21 episode of Rampage, Wayne took part in a Royal Rampage match to determine the number one contender for the AEW TNT Championship but the match was won by Darby Allin. On the September 21 episode of ROH on HonorClub, Wayne challenged Katsuyori Shibata for the ROH Pure Championship but lost. At WrestleDream, Wayne appeared during the two out of three falls match between Darby Allin and Christian Cage for the AEW TNT Championship. Wayne turned heel after hitting his friend Allin with the championship belt and helping Cage win the match. Wayne, Cage and other member Luchasaurus named their stable The Patriarchy and Wayne was known by the nickname "The Prodigy" Nick Wayne. At Holiday Bash, Cage announced that Wayne's real-life mother, Shayna, was the newest member of The Patriarchy and was named "The Matriarch" Mother Wayne. On the February 28, 2024 episode of Dynamite, Wayne challenged Orange Cassidy for the AEW International Championship but was unsuccessful. On the July 20 episode of Collision, The Patriarchy defeated the Bang Bang Gang (Austin Gunn, Colten Gunn and Juice Robinson) to win the vacant AEW World Trios Championships. This was Wayne's first championship in AEW and he also became the youngest wrestler to win a championship in the company. At All In London, The Patriarchy lost the championships in a four-way London Ladder match to the Blackpool Combat Club (Claudio Castagnoli and Wheeler Yuta). Finley is a third-generation professional wrestler. His father Buddy Wayne was an enhancement talent that made appearances for World Championship Wrestling (WCW) and World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE). His father died on June 17, 2017. His grandfather Moondog Ed Moretti made appearances in promotions around the Pacific Northwest.

Nick Schmaltz (born February 23, 1996) is an American professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Utah Mammoth of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Chicago Blackhawks and Arizona Coyotes. Before playing in the NHL, Schmaltz played three seasons with the Green Bay Gamblers of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and two years with the North Dakota Fighting Hawks of the National Collegiate Hockey Conference (NCHC). He had a successful time with his teams. He was named to the All-Rookie Teams with both the Gamblers and North Dakota. He was drafted 20th overall by the Chicago Blackhawks in the 2014 NHL entry draft. On June 19, 2016, Schmaltz signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Blackhawks. On October 12, 2016, Schmaltz made his NHL debut in a 5–2 loss against the St. Louis Blues. Three days later on October 15, Schmaltz scored his first NHL goal against Marek Mazanec in a 5–3 win against the Nashville Predators. On November 25, 2018, the Blackhawks traded Schmaltz to the Arizona Coyotes in exchange for Dylan Strome and Brendan Perlini. On March 30, 2019, Schmaltz signed a seven-year, $40.95 million contract to stay with the Coyotes. On January 26, 2023, Schmaltz recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 5–0 win against the St. Louis Blues. After the Coyotes franchise was suspended, Schmaltz and the rest of the roster were transferred to the new expansion team Utah Hockey Club. On March 11, 2026, Schmaltz signed an eight-year, $64 million contract to stay with the Mammoth. Reinier Johannes Maria "Nico" Rijnders (30 July 1947 – 16 March 1976) was a Dutch footballer. He played for NAC Breda and Ajax Amsterdam. He was part of their European Cup victory in 1971. He earned 8 caps for the Netherlands national football team. He collapsed on 12 November 1972 while playing for Club Brugge against RFC Liège. He was clinically dead when he was carried off the pitch. He was successfully reanimated by the club doctor but the incident ended Rijnders' playing career. His health never fully recovered. He died three years later at age 28. He was widely regarded to be one of the best defensive midfielders ever. He was renowned as a playmaker who knew how to make assists, pace, dribbling, man-marking and tackling. Rijnders was born on July 30, 1947 in Breda. Rijnders registered with VV Baronie in 1958. As a youth player he made the switch to fellow town NAC in 1963. He made his debut on May 16, 1965. In a cup match against Enschedese Boys. He made the winning goal 2-1 in the last minute. After a year in the First Division, promotion was won in 1966. Rijnders lost the cup final with NAC in 1967. Because winner Ajax was also national champion, the team qualified for European football. With Rijnders in the field, NAC played against Floriana FC and Cardiff City. It was a difficult season for NAC in which relegation was narrowly avoided. After the season, Rijnders moved to sub-topper Go Ahead Eagles for a transfer fee of 150,000 guilders. Rijnders developed further with the Deventer team. Rijnders went from Go Ahead to Ajax for 400,000 guilders in 1969. In his first season, the he became national champion and cup winner with Ajax. The following year, the Amsterdam team again won the cup. They also won the European Cup. Panathinaikos was defeated at Wembley. In this match, Rijnders suffered from tightness in his chest. He was replaced at half time by Horst Blankenburg. Rijnders played 63 league matches for Ajax in two seasons, in which he scored four times. Rijnders left for FC Brugge in the summer of 1971. They offered him a better contract than Ajax wanted to give him. Later it was suggested that the Ajax board led by Jaap van Praag was aware of his heart problems and therefore made little effort to keep him. Rijnders did well in Bruges and had a permanent base place. The team played in the UEFA Cup. They finished second in the league, behind Anderlecht in the 1971–72 season. On 12 November 1972, Rijnders collapsed after ten minutes on the field during a home game against Club Liège. Rijnders was clinically dead. He was resuscitated by the club doctor Michel D'Hooghe. He spent weeks in hospital. Later, he retired from professional football. He then became an assistant coach at Club Brugge. In October 1968 he was first included in the selection of the Netherlands national team by national coach Georg Keẞler. He had previously played for the Dutch military team of coach Jan Zwartkruis. On April 16, 1969, he made his debut for the Orange squad, in a friendly against Czechoslovakia. Rijnders was in the Netherlands national team in 1969 and 1970 and appeared in eight international matches. After November 1970 he disappeared from the base under the new national coach František Fadrhonc. In 1974 Rijnders became coach of the fourth division team Racing Harelbek. After new heart problems on Christmas Eve 1974, he was disqualified from all sports activities, including coaching. In July 1975, Ajax and Club Brugge organized a benefit match for Rijnders. Bruges was reinforced for the occasion with Johan Neeskens and Johan Cruijff played along with Ajax. The match ended in 3-0 for Bruges. Rijnders also opened a sports shop in Bruges. The business soon went bankrupt. Rijnders' wife left him and is said to have had a drinking problem. On March 3, 1976, he became unwell while celebrating carnival in Deventer. After a few days in a Deventer hospital he came to. Rijnders died on March 16, 1976, alone in Bruges, in his home above his old sports shop, from a heart condition. He was 28 years old. A cardiologist who treated Rijnders reported in 2009 on the basis of the medical file that the footballer suffered from congenital heart rhythm disorders. In 1976 these could not be determined and could not be remedied. In 2020, the municipality of Amsterdam named a bridge in Park de Meer after him.

Niclas Anders Hävelid (born 12 April 1973) is a Swedish former professional ice hockey defenceman. He played parts of 10 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim, Atlanta Thrashers, and New Jersey Devils. Outside of the NHL, Hävelid played for AIK IF, MIF Redhawks, Södertälje SK, and Linköpings HC of the Elitserien. Internationally, Hävelid played for Sweden and won the gold medal with them in 2006. Before playing in the NHL, Hävelid played parts of seven seasons with AIK IF and one season with MIF Redhawks of the Elitserien. He was drafted 83rd overall by the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim in the 1999 NHL entry draft. On October 2, 1999, Hävelid made his NHL debut in a 2–0 loss against the Dallas Stars. On November 19, 1999, he recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Marty McInnis goal. The next period, Hävelid scored his first NHL goal against Jocelyn Thibault in a 4–2 win against the Chicago Blackhawks. During a game against the Pittsburgh Penguins on January 15, 2001, Hävelid tore his anterior cruciate ligament and partially tore his medial collateral ligament. The injury caused him to miss 35 regular season games. On September 5, 2001, Hävelid signed a two-year contract to stay with the Mighty Ducks. He helped the Mighty Ducks when they went on a run during the Stanley Cup playoffs. The team defeated the Detroit Red Wings, Dallas Stars, and Minnesota Wild. They were eventually defeated by the New Jersey Devils four games to three in the Final. On August 6, 2003, Hävelid signed a three-year contract to stay with the Mighty Ducks. On June 26, 2004, the Mighty Ducks traded Hävelid to the Atlanta Thrashers in exchange for Kurtis Foster. He finished the 2005–06 season by scoring 4 goals and recording 28 assists for 32 points. The Thrashers awarded Hävelid for being the player who "best embodies perseverance, dedication and hard work without reward or recognition, so that his team and teammates might succeed." On June 7, 2006, Hävelid signed a three-year contract to stay with the Thrashers. On October 2, 2007, the Thrashers named Hävelid as an alternate captain of the team. During the 2006–07 season, Hävelid was able to help the Thrashers reach their first-ever playoffs. The Thrashers went on to be defeated by the New York Rangers four games to zero in the first round. It was the first and last time in the Thrashers history that they reached the playoffs. On March 2, 2009, the Thrashers traded Hävelid along with Myles Stoesz to the New Jersey Devils in exchange for Anssi Salmela. He played 15 regular season games with the Devils, recording 4 assists. On May 14, 2009, Hävelid decided to leave North America and signed a one-year contract to join Linköpings HC of the Elitserien. He played parts of four season with the team. On April 24, 2013, Hävelid announced that he was retiring from playing professional ice hockey.

She won the British Open title in 2005, 2006 and 2008. She also won the World Open title in 2005, 2006, 2008 and 2009. Nicol is the first squash player to have won the World Junior title twice; in 1999 and 2001. She was the only female squash player to have done this until in 2007. This was when Raneem El Weleily won her second World Junior Championship. Nicol joined WISPA and turned professional in 2000 when she won her first WISPA title, after only a month in the tour. The win came in February, when she beats Salma Shabana in the final of the Savcor Finnish Open. On June 7, 2008, Nicol David was recognized with the Order of Merit (Darjah Bakti) or D.B. in conjunction with the birthday of the His Majesty Tuanku Mizan Zainal Abidin. She was the first recipient of the award which was started on June 26, 1975. Nicol was also invited to carry the Olympic torch for Malaysia during the build up to the Athens Olympics in 2004 and being appointed as UNDP National Goodwill Ambassador for Malaysia. Nicol David's other notable achievements include the Asian Squash Championship, which she won with a record of seven times (in 1998, 2000, 2002, 2004, 2006, 2008 and 2010). She also held a 13-month, 51-match winning streak, from March 2006 until April 2007. In April 2007 she finally lost to Natalie Grinham in the final of the 2007 Seoul Open. Nicol has also won the WISPA Player of the Year on five consecutive times, from 2005 until 2009.

Due to being a successful model, McLean appeared on multiple reality TV shows including I'm a Celebrity...Get Me Out of Here 2008 and also appeared Celebrity Big Brother twice, in 2012 and 2017. McLean is married to footballer Tom Williams and they have two sons. Her family is Scottish.

Nicola Jupp (born 26 October 1975) is a British rugby union player. She competed in heptathlon. She competed at the 2002 Women's Rugby World Cup winning silver medal. and 2003 Women's Six Nations. She played for Richmond RFC.

Nicola Chirinsky Pietrangeli (; born Chirinsky; 11 September 1933 – 1 December 2025) was an Italian tennis player. He won two singles titles at the French Championships. He was thought by many to be one of Italy's greatest tennis champions. He was born in Tunis, then-French Tunisia to Italian parents. Pietrangeli won the French Open twice in 1958 and 1959. He made it to the quarter final of the Australian Open in 1957. He made it to the semifinal of the Wimbledon Championships in 1960. He also competed for the US Open in 1955 and 1965. After retiring as a player, Pietrangeli became Italy's Davis Cup team captain and led them to winning their first-ever Davis Cup in 1976. Pietrangeli was honored in the International Tennis Hall of Fame in 1986. On his 73rd birthday, the old tennis stadium in Foro Italico of Rome was named in his honour. Pietrangeli died in Rome, Italy on 1 December 2025 from problems caused by a fractured hip at the age of 92.

Nicolas Anelka (born 14 March 1979) is a French football manager and former player. He plays for Chelsea and France national team. Anelka started his career at Trappes Saint Quentin. But before moving to Chelsea he has played for big teams like Paris Saint-Germain, Arsenal, Real Madrid, Liverpooland Manchester City.

Nicolas Berejny (born 27 June 1968) is a skier from France. He has a disability. He skied at the 2011 IPC Alpine Skiing World Championships and was the first skier to finish in the visually impaired men's downhill race. He was the third skier to finish in the men's visually impaired Super-G race. Because he cannot see, Gregory Nouhaud was his guide and told him where to go when going down the mountain.

Nicole Bass-Fuchs (August 10, 1964 – February 17, 2017) was an American bodybuilder, actress, professional wrestler and manager. She worked for companies such as Extreme Championship Wrestling, World Wrestling Federation, Xtreme Pro Wrestling and the National Wrestling Alliance. She made many appearances as a guest on The Howard Stern Show. She was a member of Stern's Wack Pack. Bass was born in Queens, New York. She married Richard "Bob" Fuchs in 1985. Fuchs died in 2013. Bass was taken to the hospital in New York City after having a stroke in February 2017. She was said to be brain dead on February 16, 2017 after having a heart attack. Her life support was removed on February 17, dying at the age of 52.

Nicolas Wildhaber (8 December 1929 – 26 September 2020) was a Swiss swimmer. He competed at the 1948 Summer Olympics and the 1960 Summer Olympics. He was born in Zürich, Switzerland. Wildhaber died on 26 September 2020, aged 90.

Nicole Billa (born on 5 March 1996 in Kufstein, Austria) is an Austrian football player who currently plays for VfB Stuttgart and the Austria women's national team. Billa started playing football at the age of five. She played for her local club SV Angerberg. Till the under 15 level she played with the boys. Then she played for the women#s team. She attended the National Centre for Women's Football in St. Pölten. In addition to football, she also competed in kickboxing and is a three-time European and World Champion in the junior category. In the summer of 2010, Billa moved to FC Wacker Innsbruck. She made her debut in the ÖFB Cup in November 2010 at the age of 14. From March 2011 on she played regularly in the Bundesliga. For the 2013/14 season, Billa signed with league rival FSK St. Pölten. She won the runner-up title in 2014 and also the Austrian Cup. With 24 goals, the striker was the league's top scorer that season, ahead of Nina Burger (22 goals). She also scored the most goals in the cup with eight. For the 2015/16 season, she moved to German Bundesliga club TSG 1899 Hoffenheim. In the 2020/21 season, Billa was the Bundesliga's top scorer. Hoffenheim finished third in the league that season. In 2021, Billa was voted German Footballer of the Year. In the summer of 2024, she moved to 1. FC Köln. In the summer of 2025, she moved to second-division club VfB Stuttgart.

Nicolas Seiwald (born 4 May 2001) is an Austrian professional footballer who plays as a midfielder for Austrian Bundesliga club Red Bull Salzburg and the Austria national team. Seiwald began his career in 2009 with the youth academy of FC Red Bull Salzburg. He played his first match for FC Liefering against WSG Wattens on 24 May 2019. He made his debut for FC Red Bull Salzburg on 21 November 2020 when he was in the starting XI versus SK Sturm Graz. His international debut was on 17 August 2021 when he played versus Brøndby IF in a Uefa Championsleague qualifing match. After the 2022-23 season he moved to RB Leipzig. Seiwald played for all Austrian youth nationalteams. In November 2021 he was part of the A-national team. His debut was also in November 2021 when he was in the starting XI versus Israel. Scores and results list Austria's goal tally first, score column indicates score after each Seiwald goal.

Nicolás Capaldo Taboas (born 14 September 1998) is an Argentine professional footballer who plays as a midfielder for club Hamburger SV. Capaldo played in the youth of Deportivo Mac Allister. In 2015 he went on to the Boca Juniors academy. Capaldo made his debut in professional football during a Argentine Primera División match against Defensa y Justicia on 24 February 2019. In June 2021 he went on to the Austrian club Red Bull Salzburg and signed a contract to 2026. On July 10, 2025, Capaldo moved to Hamburger SV for about €4.5 million. In September 2019 he was called up in the Argentina U23s national football team. He played his first match a few days later against Colombia and scored his first goal for the team against Chile in a 1–0 win.

Nicolas Hague (born December 5, 1998) is a Canadian professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Nashville Predators of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Vegas Golden Knights. Hague is a one-time Stanley Cup champion, winning with the Golden Knights in 2023. Before playing in the NHL, Hague played three seasons with the Mississauga Steelheads of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He had a successful time with the Steelheads. He won the Max Kaminsky Trophy for being the OHL's most outstanding defenceman. He was drafted 34th overall by the Vegas Golden Knights in the 2017 NHL entry draft. On September 29, 2017, Hague signed a three-year, $2.7 million entry-level contract to join the Golden Knights. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Chicago Wolves. On October 4, 2019, the Knights called him up and Hague made his NHL debut in a 5–1 win against the San Jose Sharks. On October 12, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Cody Glass goal in a 6–2 win against the Calgary Flames. On January 21, 2020, Hague scored his first NHL goal against Jaroslav Halák in a 3–2 loss against the Boston Bruins. On October 10, 2022, Hague signed a three-year, $6.88 million contract to stay with the Knights. He helped the Golden Knights when they went on a run in the playoffs. They defeated the Winnipeg Jets, Edmonton Oilers, and Dallas Stars. They went on to defeat the Florida Panthers four games to one in the Final to win the first Stanley Cup in Golden Knights franchise history. On June 30, 2025, the Golden Knights traded Hague along with a 2027 conditional third-round draft pick to the Nashville Predators in exchange for Jérémy Lauzon and Colton Sissons. Hague signed a four-year, $22 million contract the same day to stay with the Predators.

Nicolas Aubé-Kubel (born May 10, 1996) is a Canadian professional ice hockey right winger. He currently plays for HC Dinamo Minsk of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). He has also played for the Philadelphia Flyers, Colorado Avalanche, Toronto Maple Leafs, Washington Capitals, Buffalo Sabres, New York Rangers, and Minnesota Wild of the National Hockey League (NHL). Aubé-Kubel is a one-time Stanley Cup champion, winning with the Avalanche in 2022. Before playing in the NHL, Aubé-Kubel played four seasons with the Val-d'Or Foreurs of the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League (QMJHL). He was drafted 48th overall by the Philadelphia Flyers of the 2014 NHL entry draft. On October 2, 2014, Aubé-Kubel signed an three-year entry-level contract to join the Flyers. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliates Lehigh Valley Phantoms. On October 30, 2018, the Knights called him up and Aubé-Kubel made his NHL debut in a 3–2 win against the Anaheim Ducks. On December 15, 2019, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Shayne Gostisbehere goal in a 5–2 win against the Vancouver Canucks. On December 23, Aubé-Kubel scored his first NHL goal on the powerplay against Henrik Lundqvist in a 5–1 win against the New York Rangers. On July 16, 2019, Aubé-Kubel signed a one-year contract to stay with the Flyers. On September 17, 2020, Aubé-Kubel signed a two-year, $2.15 million contract to stay with the Flyers. On November 13, 2021, the Flyers placed Aubé-Kubel onto waivers and his contract was picked up by the Colorado Avalanche. He helped the Avalanche during the playoffs. They defeated the Nashville Predators, St. Louis Blues, and Edmonton Oilers. They went on to defeat the Tampa Bay Lightning four games to two in the Final to win the Stanley Cup. On July 13, 2022, Aubé-Kubel signed a one-year, $1 million contract to join the Toronto Maple Leafs. He played 6 regular season games with the Leafs. On November 4, 2022, the Leafs placed Aubé-Kubel onto waivers and his contract was picked up by the Washington Capitals the next day. On March 3, 2023, Aubé-Kubel signed a two-year, $2.15 million contract to stay with the Capitals. On July 1, 2024, Aubé-Kubel signed a one-year, $1.5 million contract to join the Buffalo Sabres. He scored one goal and recorded one assist in 19 regular season games with the Sabres. On March 7, 2025, the Sabres traded Aubé-Kubel to the New York Rangers in exchange for Erik Brännström. He played three regular season games with the Rangers. On July 2, 2025, Aubé-Kubel signed a one-year, two-way $775,000 contract to join the Minnesota Wild. He recorded two assists in six games for the Wild.

Nicolas Roy (born February 5, 1997) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the Colorado Avalanche of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Carolina Hurricanes, Vegas Golden Knights, and Toronto Maple Leafs. Roy is a one-time Stanley Cup champion, winning with the Golden Knights in 2023. Before playing in the NHL, Roy played four seasons with the Chicoutimi Saguenéens of the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League (QMJHL). He had a successful time with the Saguenéens. He won the Guy Carbonneau Trophy as the best defensive forward in the QMJHL and was named to back-to-back First All-Star Teams. He also played in the CHL/NHL Top Prospects Game. He was drafted 96th overall by the Carolina Hurricanes of the 2015 NHL entry draft. On April 9, 2016, Roy signed an three-year, $1.875 million entry-level contract to join the Hurricanes. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliates Charlotte Checkers. On April 7, 2018, the Hurricanes called him up and Roy made his NHL debut in a 3–2 overtime win against the Tampa Bay Lightning. On October 27, 2019, Roy scored his first NHL goal against Marc-André Fleury in a 5–2 win against the Anaheim Ducks. On June 26, 2019, the Hurricanes traded Roy along with a 2021 conditional fifth-round draft pick to the Vegas Golden Knights in exchange for Erik Haula. On April 22, 2020, Roy signed a two-year contract to stay with the Knights. He helped the Knights during the playoffs. They defeated the Winnipeg Jets, Edmonton Oilers, and Dallas Stars. They went on to defeat the Florida Panthers four games to one in the Final to win the first Stanley Cup in Golden Knights franchise history. On April 22, 2020, Roy signed a five-year, $15 million contract to stay with the Knights. On July 1, 2025, the Knights traded Roy to the Toronto Maple Leafs in exchange for Mitch Marner. He scored 5 goals and recorded 15 assists in 59 regular season games with the Leafs. On March 5, 2026, the Leafs traded Roy to the Colorado Avalanche in exchange for a 2026 conditional fifth-round draft pick and a 2027 conditional first-round draft pick. He scored 5 goals and recorded 15 assists in 59 regular season games with the Leafs.

Nicole Vaidišová (born 23 April 1989 in Nuremberg) is a Czech professional female tennis player. She became a tennis professional in 2003, and debuted in several ITF tournaments. She measures at and weighs 139 lb. She enjoys reading, watching movies, yoga, and bike riding. Her favorite city is New York City. She speaks German, English, Czech, and is learning French.

Nicole Brown Simpson (May 19, 1959 – June 12, 1994) was a German-American model. She was the ex-wife of retired professional football player and actor O. J. Simpson. They were married from 1985 to 1992. She was the mother of their two children, Sydney and Justin. She was murdered at her home in Los Angeles, California, on June 12, 1994, along with her friend, restaurant waiter Ron Goldman, two years after her divorce from Simpson. This led to the controversial criminal trial of Simpson.

Nicole Lewis (born 26 January 1989) is a New Zealand female water polo player. She competed for the New Zealand women's national water polo team in the 2013 World Aquatics Championships, 2015 World Aquatics Championships, and 2017 World Aquatics Championships.

Nicole Oude Luttikhuis (born 26 December 1997) is a Dutch volleyball player. She was in the Netherlands women's national volleyball team. She participated in the 2015 Montreux Volley Masters and 2015 European Games.

Nicoletta Abbate is an Italian water polo player. She was a member of the Italian women's national water polo team. She played at the 1989 European Water Polo Championship, 1991 European Water Polo Championship, and 1994 World Aquatics Championships.
Nicole Koller (born 2 May 1997 in Wetzikon) is a Swiss road racing cyclist. She competed at the 2021 UCI Road World Championships, in the mixed team relay event and women's road race event.

Nicole Louise Frain (born 24 August 1992) is an Australian professional racing cyclist from Tasmania, who currently rides for the Dutch UCI Women's Continental Team Parkhotel Valkenburg Cycling Team. Frain won the silver medal at the 2019 Oceania Road Cycling Championships in the time trial event. In 2021 Frain won the bronze medal at the Australian National Time Trial Championships. She became the 2022 Australian National Road Race Champion. She competed at the 2022 Tour de France Femmes. In the second stage she rode with high speed into Marta Cavalli causing a crash. The way she rode into Cavalli was mentioned as careless cycling and caused commotion. Cavalli had to leave the Tour. Especially since after the fall and while Marta Cavalli was lying on the ground suffering from a concussion, she did not take care of her condition, picking up her bike and resuming her race. This fall put an end to the form of Marta Cavalli, who was one of the best cyclists in the world at that time and who had just won the Flèche Wallone and the Amstel Gold Race in the spring. After this fall, Marta Cavalli was never able to resume her career, and announced her retirement in 2025, exhausted from training to regain a form that never returned. In 2014, Frain was involved in a traffic accident killing a 78-year-old man. Frain was said to have been fallen asleep while driven. She got a suspended sentence for this accident.

Nicolo Turco (15 January 2004 in Tortona) is an Italian football player. He plays as forward for the Austrian 2nd league team FC Liefering on loan from FC Red Bull Salzburg. Turco started his career at CFC Genoa. For the 2018/19 season he went to the youth team of Juventus Turin. He played for the Primavera team from the 2021/22 season on. He also played in the 2021/22 and 2022/23 UEFA Youth League seasons. In July 2023, he went to the Austrian Bundesliga club FC Red Bull Salzburg. In Salzburg he was loaned to FC Liefering. He made his debut in the second division in the same month when he came on for Luka Reischl in the 45th minute against FC Dornbirn 1913 on the first day of the 2023/24 season. In August 2024, Turco returned to Italy on loan. He mo toved AC Milan's third-tier reserves. Turco played for an Italian youth national team for the first time in February 2019. In September 2022 he made his debut for the U-19 team. With that he also took part in the EM in 2023. He became European champion with Italy. He played in all games except the final.

Nicolino Locche (September 2, 1939 – September 7, 2005) was an Argentine professional boxer from Tunuyán, Mendoza who held the World Junior Welterweight title from 1968 to 1972. Locche turned professional at the age of 19 and amassed a record of 117-4-14 (14 draws). He had several successful defenses including one over Antonio Cervantes. Regarded as one of the greatest defensive boxers of all time, his way of frustrating his foes with a minimum of head movement and avoiding most of their punches earned him the moniker El Intocable (the Untouchable). He was inducted into the International Boxing Hall Of Fame in 2003. Locche died in Las Heras in 2005 of heart failure.

Nicolás Andrés Burdisso (born 12 April 1981) is an Argentine sporting director and former professional footballer who played as a centre back. Scores and results list Argentina's goal tally first. Primera División: 2000 Apertura, 2003 Apertura Serie A: 2005–06, 2006–07, 2007–08, 2008–09

Nicolás Fuentes Fuentes (20 February 1941 – 28 October 2015) was a Peruvian football player. Fuentes made 17 appearances for the Peru national football team from 1965 to 1971, including playing at the 1970 FIFA World Cup. Fuentes died from respiratory failure caused by diabetes in Lima, Peru, aged 74.

Niculae Nedeff (September 26, 1928 – July 24, 2017) was a Romanian handball player and coach of the Romania women's national handball team and Romania national handball team. He won the World Championships seven times, three times with the girls' team and four times with the boys' team. He was born in Bucharest. After retiring, he joined the Executive Committee of the Romanian Olympic Committee. Nedeff died on July 24, 2017 in Bucharest at the age of 88.

Nicolás Santiago Keenan (born 6 May 1997) is an Argentine field hockey player. He plays as a midfielder or forward for Dutch Hoofdklasse club Klein Zwitserland. He has also played for the Argentina national team since 2019. Keenan was born in Buenos Aires, Argentina, and grew up in Spain and Italy. Keenan is bisexual and has been in a relationship with Prime Minister of the Netherlands Rob Jetten since 2022. They announced their engagement in November 2024.

Niels Holst-Sørensen (19 December 1922 – 24 October 2023) was a Danish athlete and air force officer. He was the commander-in-chief of the Royal Danish Air Force between 1970 until 1982. He was Denmark's military representative to NATO between 1982 until 1986. He won gold and silver medals at the 1946 European Athletics Championships. He was a member of the International Olympic Committee from 1977 to 2002. He died died on 24 October 2023, at the age of 100.

Nigel Howard Clough (born 19 March 1966) is an English professional football manager and former player who is currently the manager of Mansfield Town. Clough is most famous for his time at Nottingham Forest, where he scored 131 goals in over 400 games. He is the second highest scoring player in the history of the team. Northern Premier League Premier Division: 2001–02 Southern League Championship Shield: 2000 Bass Charity Vase: 2002, 2003, 2004, 2005, 2006, 2007, 2008 Southern League Premier Division Runners-up: 1999–2000, 2000–2001 Football League One Manager of the Month: February 2014

Nigel Howard Adkins (born 11 March 1965) is an English football manager and former footballer. He is currently the manager and technical director at Tranmere Rovers. Adkins played for Tranmere Rovers, Wigan Athletic and Bangor City. Adkins' career as a manager started with Bangor City. From 1996 to 2006 he worked for Scunthorpe United as a physiotherapist. He worked for Scunthorpe United as a main coach for four years. In 2010, Adkins became the main coach of Southampton. In March 2013, Adkins became a main coach of Reading.

Nigel Ernest James Mansell OBE (born 8 August 1953 in Upton-upon-Severn, Worcestershire) is a British racing driver from England who won both the Formula One World Championship (1992) and CART World Series (1993). He is the only person in history to hold both titles simultaneously, and was the first person to win the CART title in his debut season. During the early nineties, Mansell was commonly known, by the British media especially, as Our Nige. His career in Formula One spanned 15 seasons, with his final two full seasons of top-level racing being spent in the CART series. Mansell remains the second most successful British Formula One driver of all-time in terms of race wins with 31 victories, only behind Lewis Hamilton. He is eighth overall on the Formula One race winners list. He was rated in the top 10 Formula One drivers of all time by Murray Walker, who was a Formula One commentator for 50 years. In 2008, American sports television network ESPN ranked him 24th on their top drivers of all-time. Mansell raced in the GP Masters series and signed a one-off race deal for the Scuderia Ecosse GT race team to drive their number 63 Ferrari430 GT2 car at Silverstone on 6 May 2007.

Nigel Shola Andre Reo-Coker (born 14 May 1984) is an English former professional footballer who played as a midfielder, as well as a football commentator and pundit for CBS Sports. Football League Championship play-offs: 2004–05 CONCACAF Champions League runner-up: 2014–15

Nigel de Jong (; born 30 November 1984) is a Dutch former professional footballer. He joined the Ajax youth academy when he was young and made the first team at age 17. De Jong moved from Ajax in 2006 to join Hamburg. He then moved to Manchester City in January 2009 for around £18 million. He became an important part of Manchester City's midfield. He has earned a reputation of being combative and feisty player. This got him nicknames like "The Terrier" and "Lawnmower". He moved to Italian club Milan in August 2012. On 19 October 2002, de Jong played for the Ajax first team for the first time. He scored his first goal on 18 February 2003 in a 1–1 draw against Arsenal in the UEFA Champions League. He started playing in the first team often in the next season. In this season, Ajax won the Eredivisie. In 2004–05, de Jong was named Ajax Player of the Season. Later, after starting in midfield for quite a while, he found himself sitting on the bench more often than being one of the players at the start of a match. On 7 December 2005, it was announced that de Jong did not want to stay with Ajax. His contract with Ajax was due to finish in July 2006. On 26 January 2006, de Jong signed a four and a half year contract at German Bundesliga club Hamburg. He moved there for about €1 million. He played for Hamburg for the first time two days later. In the match, Hamburg lost 2–1 to Nuremberg. In March 2006, de Jong scored the winning goal in Bayern Munich's first ever loss at the Allianz Arena. The week after, he got his first red card in a UEFA Cup match against Rapid Bucharest. He had to stop playing in April because he needed surgery on a knee problem. The injury also meant that he could not play for the Netherlands at the 2006 World Cup. However, after becoming fit again, he was put on standby. On 21 January 2009, de Jong moved to Manchester City for around £18 million. He signed a four-and-a-half year contract. He played for the first time against Newcastle United on 28 January 2009. He appeared sixteen times in the Premier League. De Jong was in the starting team against Arsenal on 12 September 2009. He was given Man of the Match by Sky Sports after Manchester City won 2-1 over Chelsea on 5 December 2009. By the end of the season, the fans liked him. He was one of Roberto Mancini's first picks as defensive midfielder as the team just missed out on the Champions League. De Jong scored his first goal for Manchester City when they won 2-1 against West Ham United on 1 May 2011. On 31 August 2012, de Jong joined Italian Serie A club Milan. He signed a three-year contract. On 31 March 2004, de Jong played his first game with the Netherlands in a friendly against France. He was not picked to play in UEFA Euro 2004. He missed the 2006 FIFA World Cup because his knee was injured. He scored his first goal for the Netherlands against Iceland on 6 June 2009 in a 2010 FIFA World Cup qualifying match. This match made the Netherlands go through to the 2010 World Cup. De Jong was part of the Dutch team for the 2010 FIFA World Cup. He was one of the starting players for their first match in the competition. In this match, they won 2–0 against Denmark. He was not allowed to play in the semi final against Uruguay because he got his second yellow card in a match against Brazil. He played in the Final, where the Netherlands lost 1–0 to Spain. Scores list Netherlands' tally first. FIFA World Cup runner-up: 2010; third place: 2014 Ajax Player of the Year (Rinus Michels Award): 2004–05

Nigel David Short MBE (born 1 June 1965 in Leigh, Lancashire) is often regarded as the strongest English chess player of the 20th century. He became a Grandmaster at age 19. He challenged for the World Chess Championship against Garry Kasparov at London 1993. Still active, Short continues to enjoy international success. He is also a chess columnist, coach and commentator. Short's best achievement was in the World Candidates matches of 1992, when he beat world-class players Boris Gelfand, Anatoly Karpov and Jan Timman to reach the final. In the World Championship match, London 1993, he was decisively beaten by the reigning World Champion, Gary Kasparov. The match caused controversy because the two players broke away from FIDE, for reasons mostly to do with the prize money. Short has played 21 times for England in Chess Olympiads, and European and World Team championships. He has been living in Greece with his wife and children for a number of years.

Nigel Starmer-Smith (born 25 December 1944) is a British former international rugby union player, rugby journalist and commentator. He was born in Cheltenham, England. Starmer-Smith played for the England national rugby union team between 1969 until 1971. In 2015, Starmer-Smith was diagnosed with dementia.

Steven Haworth (born 23 January 1976) is an English commentator and former professional wrestler. He currently works for All Elite Wrestling (AEW) under the ring name Nigel McGuinness as commentator for their Collision show. McGuinness is also best known for his time wrestling in Ring of Honor (ROH) and Total Nonstop Action Wrestling (TNA). He also did commentary in the WWE. During his time in ROH, McGuinness was a one-time ROH Pure Champion and a one-time ROH World Champion. In TNA, he was a member of the Fortune stable and wrestled under the ring name Desmond Wolfe. After he would contract Hepatitis B and suffered multiple concussions throughout his career, McGuinness would make the decision to retire from in-ring competition in 2011. At Supercard of Honor, McGuinness would make his surprise return to Ring of Honor (ROH). On 5 April 2023, owner Tony Khan announced that McGuinness had signed a contract with All Elite Wrestling (AEW) to become a commentator for their Collision show. He currently commentates the show alongside Tony Schiavone. On 25 August 2024 at All In in his hometown of London, McGuinness would make his in-ring return for the first time since 2011. He would compete in the Casino Gauntlet match for a future AEW World Championship match. He entered third in the match and would be eliminated by eventual winner Christian Cage. On the 11 September episode of Dynamite, McGuinness would send out a challenge to his long-term rival Bryan Danielson to face him at Grand Slam. It was later confirmed to have been accepted.

Nihel Ghoul (born 2 June 1984) is a Tunisian national volleyball player. She played at the 2014 FIVB Volleyball Women's World Championship. She graduated from University of Rouen. She played for Olympic Club of Kelibia, UGS Havre Ocean / HAC, CEP Poitiers Saint-Benoît, and Volley-ball Saint-Dié-des-Vosges.

Nika Kiladze ( 29 November 1988 – 7 October 2014) was a Georgian footballer. He played professionally in both Georgia and Finland from 2006 until his death in 2014. He played as a defensive midfielder for Orbebi Tbilisi, Kokkolan Palloveikot (KPV), Kajaanin Haka, and FC Guria Lanchkhuti. Kiladze was born in Gagra, Abkhaz ASSR, Georgian SSR of the Soviet Union. Kiladze died in a motorcycle accident on 7 October 2014 in Tbilisi. He was 25.

Nikita Vasilyevich Filatov (; born May 25, 1990) is a Russian professional ice hockey player who is currently a member of Salavat Yulaev of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). Filatov was loaned to HC CSKA Moscow of the KHL by the Ottawa Senators of the National Hockey League (NHL) in December, 2011.

Nikhil Nandy (1932 – 29 December 2020) was an Indian footballer. He competed in the men's tournament at the 1956 Summer Olympics. He played for the national team. He was born in Kolkata, India. Nandy died on 29 December 2020 in Nagerbazar, India at the age of 88.

Nikita Pavlovich Simonyan (,; 12 October 1926 – 23 November 2025) was a Soviet and Russian football striker and coach. He spent most of his career at Spartak Moscow. There, he was the top scorer of all time with 160 goals. He played for the Soviet Union national team, winning the gold medal at the 1956 Olympics. Simonyan was the Russian football First Vice-president of the Russian Football Union. On 20 November 2025, Simonyan was hospitalized in Moscow, Russia after falling and breaking his leg. He died three days later on 23 November 2025 at the age of 99.

Nikita Tolopilo (born 6 April 2000) is a Belarusian professional ice hockey goaltender. He currently plays for the Vancouver Canucks of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Chicago Blackhawks and Nashville Predators. Outside of the NHL, Tolopilo played for the Jokerit, HIFK, and KooKoo of the Liiga. Before playing in the NHL, Tolopilo played two seasons with Dinamo Minsk of the Liiga. He was not drafted by an NHL team. On 15 May 2023, Tolopilo signed a two-year, $950,000 entry-level contract to join the Vancouver Canucks of the National Hockey League (NHL). They sent him down to play for their AHL-affiliate Abbotsford Canucks. On 14 April 2025, Vancouver called him up and Tolopilo made his NHL debut, stopping 15 of 16 shots in a 2–1 overtime win against the San Jose Sharks. On 8 July, Tolopilo signed a two-year contract to stay with the Canucks. He won the Calder Cup with the Abbotsford Canucks in 2025.

Nikita Dmitrovich Chibrikov (; born October 29, 1992) is a Russian professional ice hockey right winger. He currently plays for the Winnipeg Jets of the National Hockey League (NHL). Outside of the NHL, Chibrikov has played for SKA Saint Petersburg and Spartak Moscow of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). Before playing in the NHL, Chibrikov played parts of two seasons with SKA Saint Petersburg and part of one season with Spartak Moscow of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). He was drafted 50th overall by the Winnipeg Jets in the 2021 NHL entry draft. On 1 May 2023, Chibrikov signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Jets. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Manitoba Moose. On 18 April 2024, the Jets called him up and Chibrikov made his NHL debut in a 4–2 win against the Vancouver Canucks. During the third period, Chibrikov scored his first NHL goal against Thatcher Demko which turned out to be the game-winning goal. On 5 October 2025, Chibrikov signed a two-year, $1.75 million contract to stay with the Jets.

Nikita Nesterenko (born September 10, 2001) is an American professional ice hockey center. He currently plays for the Anaheim Ducks of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Nesterenko played one season with the Chilliwack Chiefs of the British Columbia Hockey League (BCHL) and three years with the Boston College Eagles of Hockey East. He had a successful time with his teams. With the Eagles, he was named and was also named to the. He was drafted 172nd overall by the Minnesota Wild in the 2019 NHL entry draft. He never played a game for the Wild. On March 3, 2023, the Wild traded Nesterenko along with Andrej Šustr and a 2025 fourth-round draft pick to the Anaheim Ducks in exchange for John Klingberg. On March 15, 2023, Nesterenko signed a two-year entry-level contract to join the Ducks. On March 21, 2023, Nesterenko made his NHL debut in a 5–1 loss against the Calgary Flames. On March 25, Nesterenko scored his first NHL goal against Jordan Binnington in a 6–3 loss against the St. Louis Blues. On July 15, 2024, Nesterenko signed a one-year entry-level contract to stay with the Ducks. On June 18, 2025, Nesterenko signed a two-year entry-level contract to stay with the Ducks. Nesterenko was born in Brooklyn, New York and was raised in Coney Island to Russian immigrants.

Nikita Sergeevich Grebenkin (, born 2 May 2003) is a Russian professional ice hockey right winger. He currently plays for the Philadelphia Flyers of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Toronto Maple Leafs. Outside of the NHL, Grebenkin played for Metallurg Magnitogorsk and Amur Khabarovsk of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). Before playing in the NHL, Grebenkin played parts of three seasons with Metallurg Magnitogorsk and one season with Amur Khabarovsk of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). He helped Metallurg during the playoffs. They defeated Amur Khabarovsk, HC Spartak Moscow, and Avtomobilist Yekaterinburg. They went on to defeat and sweep Lokomotiv Yaroslavl four games to zero in the Final to win the Gagarin Cup. He was also named the Rookie of the Year. He was drafted 135th overall by the Toronto Maple Leafs in the 2022 NHL entry draft. On 29 April 2024, Grebenkin signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Maple Leafs. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Toronto Marlies. On 20 November 2024, the Leafs called him up and Grebenkin made his NHL debut in a 3–0 win against the Vegas Golden Knights. On 11 October 2025, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Bobby Brink goal in a 4–3 overtime loss against the Carolina Hurricanes. On 4 November, Grebenkin scored his first NHL goal against Sam Montembeault in a 5–4 shootout win against the Montreal Canadiens. On 7 March 2025, the Leafs traded Grebenkin along with a 2027 conditional first-round draft pick to the Philadelphia Flyers in exchange for Scott Laughton, a 2025 fourth-round draft pick, and a 2027 sixth-round draft pick. On 6 August 2026, Grebenkin signed a two-year, $2.2 million contract to stay with the Flyers.

Nikita Igorevich Kucherov (; born 17 June 1993) is an Russian professional ice hockey right winger. He currently plays for the Tampa Bay Lightning of the National Hockey League (NHL). Outside of the NHL, Kucherov played for CSKA Moscow of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). Kucherov is a two-time Stanley Cup champion, winning back-to-back championships with the Lightning in 2020 and 2021. He is also a three-time Art Ross Trophy winner, two-time Ted Lindsay Award winner, and a two-time Hart Memorial Trophy winner. He is a five-time All-Star, being named one in 2017, 2018, 2019, 2023, and 2024. Before playing in the NHL, Kucherov played 27 regular season games over two seasons for CSKA Moscow of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL), as well as, six regular season games with the Quebec Remparts and one season with the Rouyn-Noranda Huskies of the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League (QMJHL). He was drafted 58th overall by the Tampa Bay Lightning in the 2011 NHL entry draft. On 10 September 2012, Kucherov signed a three-year, $2.2275 million entry-level contract to join the Lightning. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Syracuse Crunch. On 25 November 2013, the Lightning called him up and Kucherov made his NHL debut in a 5–0 win against the New York Rangers. During the first period, he scored his first NHL goal against Henrik Lundqvist. On 28 October 2014, he recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 7–3 win against the Arizona Coyotes. The 2016–17 season was very successful for Kucherov. He was named the First Star of the Week three times, the Second Star of November, and the First Star of March. On 11 October 2016, Kucherov signed a three-year, $14.3 million entry-level contract to stay with the Lightning. The next season was also successful for Kucherov. On 10 January 2017, he was selected to play in his first All-Star game. He was also named a two-time Second Star of the Week, the Second Star of October, and the Third Star of December. He was named to his second All-Star game that season. On 10 July 2018, Kucherov signed an eight-year, $76 million contract to stay with the Lightning. He finished the next season scoring 41 goals and recording 87 assists for 128 points in 82 regular season games and also recorded 2 assists in 3 playoff games for the Lightning. He was awarded the Art Ross Trophy for being the league's leading point scorer, Ted Lindsay Award for most outstanding player by the NHL Players' Association, and Hart Memorial Trophy for most valuable player. He was also selected to play for his third All-Star game. He helped the Lightning during the playoffs. They defeated the Columbus Blue Jackets, Boston Bruins, and New York Islanders. They went on to defeat the Dallas Stars four games to two in the Final to win the Stanley Cup. The Lightning went on to repeat as Stanley Cup champions the next season. On 5 January 2023, he was named to his fourth All-Star game. He finished the 2023–24 season scoring 44 goals and recording 100 assists for 144 points in 81 regular season games and also recorded 7 assists in 5 playoff games for the Lightning. He was awarded his second Art Ross Trophy for being the league's leading point scorer and was named to his fifth All-Star game. His success did not stop the next season with him scoring 37 goals and recording 84 assists for 121 points in 78 regular season games and also recorded 4 assists in 5 playoff games for the Lightning. He was awarded his second straight Art Ross Trophy and was also named the winner of the Ted Lindsay Award. He finished the 2025–26 season winning his second Hart Memorial Trophy the next season.

Niklas Hjalmarsson (born June 6, 1987 in Eksjö, Sweden) is a Swedish professional ice hockey player that currently plays for the Arizona Coyotes of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for their farm team the Rockford IceHogs of the AHL and the Chicago Blackhawks (NHL). Although he spent the majority of his time on the IceHogs, He earned a regular spot on the Chicago Blackhawks roster after James Wisniewski was traded to the Anaheim Ducks. Hjalmarsson won the Stanley Cup with the Blackhawks in 2010. On July 9, 2010, He signed an offer sheet with the San Jose Sharks which was for 4 years and $14 million. The Blackhawks matched it and Hjalmarsson became the first defenceman in 13 years to receive an offer sheet as a restricted free agent. On June 24, 2013, He won his second Stanley Cup with the Blackhawks after they defeated the Boston Bruins 4 games to 2 in the 2013 Stanley Cup Finals.

Niklas Oskar Bäckström (born February 13, 1978) is a Finnish professional ice hockey goaltender. He plays for the Minnesota Wild of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played in the SM-liiga for HIFK, SaiPa and Kärpät and in the Elitserien for AIK. He won the William M. Jennings Trophy in 2007 along with Manny Fernandez. He also played for Finland at the 2006 Winter Olympics where he won a silver medal and at the 2010 Winter Olympics where he won a bronze medal.

Niklas Süle (born 3 September 1995) is a German professional footballer who plays as a centre-back or right-back for the club Borussia Dortmund and the Germany national team. Niklas "Nikke" Kokko (born 14 March 2004) is a Finnish professional ice hockey goaltender. He currently plays for the Seattle Kraken of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the New York Rangers. Outside of the NHL, Kokko has also played for Oulun Kärpät, SaiPa, and the Lahti Pelicans of the Liiga. Before playing in the NHL, Kokko played three seasons with Oulun Kärpät, one season with SaiPa, and one season with the Lahti Pelicans of the Liiga. He was drafted 58th overall by the Seattle Kraken in the 2022 NHL entry draft. On July 24, 2014, Kokko signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Kraken. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Coachella Valley Firebirds On 25 February 2025, Kokko made his NHL debut, coming in relief of Joey Daccord and stopping 4 of 6 shots he faced in a 7–2 loss against the St. Louis Blues. On 11 April 2026, Kokko started his first NHL game, stopping 26 of 27 shots he faced in a 4–1 win against the Calgary Flames.

Nikita Sergeyevich Zadorov (; born 16 April 1995) is a Russian professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Boston Bruins of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Buffalo Sabres, Colorado Avalanche, Chicago Blackhawks, Calgary Flames, and Vancouver Canucks. Before playing in the NHL, Zadorov played two seasons with London Knights of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He had a successful time with the Knights. He was named to both the First All-Rookie Team and Second All-Star Team. He also played in the CHL/NHL Top Prospects Game. He was drafted 16th overall by the Buffalo Sabres in the 2013 NHL entry draft. On 25 September 2013, Zadorov signed a three-year, $2.775 million entry-level contract to join the Sabres. On 19 October 2013, Zadorov made his NHL debut in a 4–2 loss against the Colorado Avalanche. Four days later on 23 October 2013, Zadorov scored his first NHL goal against Chad Johnson in a 5–2 loss against the Boston Bruins. On 26 June 2015, the Sabres traded Zadorov along with Mikhail Grigorenko, J. T. Compher, and a 2015 second-round draft pick to the Colorado Avalanche in exchange for Ryan O'Reilly and Jamie McGinn. On 15 September 2017, Zadorov signed a two-year, $4.3 million contract to stay with the Avalanche. On 5 July 2019, Zadorov signed a one-year, $3.2 million contract to stay with the Avalanche. On 9 October 2020, the Avalanche traded Zadorov along with Anton Lindholm to the Chicago Blackhawks in exchange for Brandon Saad and Dennis Gilbert. He scored 1 goal and recorded 7 assists in 55 regular season games for the Blackhawks. On 28 July 2021, the Blackhawks traded Zadorov to the Calgary Flames in exchange for a 2022 third-round draft pick. On 20 August, Zadorov signed a one-year, $3.75 million contract to stay with the Flames. On 13 July 2022, Zadorov signed a two-year, $7.5 million contract to stay with the Flames. On 12 April 2023, he recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 4–3 loss against the San Jose Sharks. On 30 November 2023, the Flames traded Zadorov to the Vancouver Canucks in exchange for a 2024 conditional fifth-round draft pick and a 2026 third-round draft pick. He scored 5 goals and recorded 9 assists in 54 regular season games. He also scored 4 goals and recorded 4 assists in 13 playoff games for the Canucks. On 1 July 2024, Zadorov signed a six-year, $30 million contract to join the Boston Bruins. Zadorov has been vocal about his opposition to the Russian invasion of Ukraine and said that he is unlikely welcomed back in Russia.
